context_facts.text: For the average US household, food production dominates food-related emissions (83%); transport as a whole is about 11% of life-cycle emissions and final delivery from producer to retail only 4% (Weber & Matthews 2008, Environ. Sci. Technol., doi:10.1021/es702969f).

care: Water well: newly planted figs dry out easily.
Mulch each spring to keep in moisture and stop weeds.
In cold places, protect the fig over winter.
Plant in a warm, sunny, sheltered spot, such as a south-facing wall.

size.basis: Fan-trained on a wall: about 1.8 m tall and 3.5 m wide (RHS). A free-standing tree in a warm climate: up to 10 m tall and 4.5–9 m wide (Gardening Australia).

care: Water your young tree through the warm months while it settles in.
Plant it in a sunny spot with soil that drains well.
Protect young plants from frost; older trees cope with light frost.
Keep a weed-free circle with mulch around the trunk, not touching it.

visual.leaf: Shiny, leathery evergreen leaves, oval with a long point and wavy, toothed edges.
visual.fruit: Round woody brown capsules that split into five parts in autumn.
visual.flower: White five-petalled flowers with many yellow stamens, in clusters at branch tips (June to August).
visual.notes: Tall evergreen; planted on Hong Kong hills as a fire-resistant tree. Its bark can irritate skin.

tree.small_note: Schima grows into a tall evergreen tree, so it suits parks, hillsides and big gardens.
tree.wildlife: Schima's white summer flowers attract bees and scarab beetles.

care: Water your young tree through the warm months while it settles in.
Keep a weed-free circle about 1 m wide, with a mulch about 10 cm deep.
Fit a guard round the trunk if rabbits or other animals nibble bark.
If you used a stake, take it away after two to three years.
